messages:
maya: Quick note from onboarding reranker-v7: after candidate priming (we prepend short snippets from doc titles) and int4 PTQ, overall NDCG up but MRR@1 on canonical-title queries drops ~0.05.

alex: By candidate priming you mean we added a short title-context token to each candidate string before scoring? Could be shifting score mass to title features.

maya: Exactly. Example: candidate before: "How to reset nginx" -> after priming: "[TITLE] Nginx: resetting service - How to reset nginx". Float baseline w/ priming: MRR@1=0.392, int4+priming: MRR@1=0.343. No-priming float/int4 deltas small.

rachel: So priming amplifies some features and quant noise seems to hurt those amplified directions more. Do we have margin histograms per-config?

maya: Pasted quick stats: median margin (gt - runnerup): float+priming=1.15, int4+priming=0.48. tail<=0.1 fraction: float+priming=7%, int4+priming=19%.

eval-bot: run 3311112233 complete. full eval NDCG@10: float=0.418 int4=0.427 (+0.009). MRR@1: float=0.399 int4=0.354 (-0.045). primed-canonical subset shows most drop.

alex: Two possibilities: (1) priming creates new high-correlation tokens that are sensitive to quant noise; (2) tokenizer/subtoken boundary changes due to added prefix cause shifts. Have you verified tokenizer parity across runs after priming?

maya: Tokenizer parity checked and stable. The prefix is identical between float and int4 runs. I also sham-ran a control where we add an unrelated prefix like "[META]" and the int4 drop is much smaller. So likely content-specific feature directions.

rachel: Ablation ideas: (A) calibrate int4 with a primed-heavy sample (include many primed candidates), (B) try symmetric per-channel scaling, (C) run post-quant bias-remedy, (D) small loss-aware PTQ tuning on a primed-golden 500 examples focusing on top1 preservation. Also test removing title tokens from candidates and compute delta to isolate effect.

alex: Also consider soft-label distillation during PTQ: use float logits as teacher for calibration loss to preserve relative ordering when priming increases co-linearity.

maya: Good call. I'll queue ablations A-D and the distillation cal run. Also adding a candidate-format bucket to the eval (primed vs canonical vs truncated) to track where mass moves. Seeds set to 777 for parity.

eval-bot: queued ablation runs: 3311112235 (A), 3311112240 (B), 3311112245 (C), 3311112248 (D), 3311112249 (distill). Will report compact numbers when finished.

ops-bot: note: when running primed-heavy calibration, ensure batching and kvpack match production; otherwise calibration stats will mismatch.

rachel: If distillation or primed-aware calibration fixes it, add "candidate-format calibration" to the onboarding checklist and require primed-candidate smoke runs for any feature that mutates candidate text.

maya: Agreed. If none of these fix it, fallback plan is to move priming into a reranker-agnostic post-process (e.g., rerank unprimed, then re-score with priming for presentation) but prefer fixing quant pipeline.

alex: One more quick check: do logits compress uniformly or is it mainly specific heads/layers? Can you dump per-layer activation norm change after quant for primed examples?

maya: I'll include that in debugging logs for a few representative queries. Posting numbers-only summary when runs finish.

eval-bot: reminder: original float baseline seed=77. Ensure all ablation runs use seed=777 and report seed in summaries.

maya: Thanks team. Will open a short onboarding PR to add candidate-format calibration if ablation shows it's necessary. Keeping this thread for final numbers and next steps only.
